think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 70-year-old woman from India presenting with profound constitutional symptoms (anorexia, weight loss, weakness) is found on cross-sectional imaging to have an ill-defined 24-mm mass in the pancreatic neck invading the duodenum with regional lymphadenopathy. The clinical picture is virtually indistinguishable from primary pancreatic adenocarcinoma, but represents tuberculous pseudotumor with duodenal fistulization in the context of newly detected advanced immunosuppression.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission narrative halts following the outpatient/emergency presentation, constitutional symptom timeline, initial abdominal/pelvic CT demonstrating the 24-mm mass in the pancreatic neck with portacaval/retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, and endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) demonstrating the mixed solid-cystic mass with duodenal fistula, immediately prior to pancreatic tissue biopsy, AFB stains, MTB cultures, tuberculin testing, HIV viral load/CD4 testing, and antimycobacterial therapy.
3. Differential Distinctions: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is the primary suspect in an elderly patient with painless jaundice, constitutional wasting, and a mass invading the duodenum, but tissue biopsy shows necrotizing granulomas rather than malignant adenocarcinoma cells. Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor or cystic neoplasm presents as a circumscribed or cystic pancreatic mass, but does not spontaneously fistulize with purulent drainage and lacks caseating granulomatous inflammation. Disseminated mycobacteriosis can manifest primarily as an isolated pancreatic or peripancreatic mass in patients from endemic areas.
case_prompt:
A 70-year-old woman with a history of hypothyroidism presents for evaluation of progressive, unintentional weight loss, profound anorexia, intermittent nausea and vomiting, headaches, generalized myalgias, and debilitating weakness. She is a homemaker originally from India who travels regularly, residing in the United States for six months of each year. Her symptoms have worsened over several weeks, leading to significant functional decline.

On physical examination, she appears chronologically aged, chronically ill, and cachectic. Vital signs are stable without acute hypoxemia or hypotension. Abdominal examination is remarkable for mild generalized epigastric discomfort on deep palpation without guarding, rebound tenderness, or palpable organomegaly. No peripheral lymphadenopathy or cutaneous lesions are identified.

A contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) scan of the abdomen and pelvis reveals a 24 mm x 23 mm x 19 mm ill-defined soft tissue mass inseparable from the pancreatic neck and the medial wall of the descending duodenum, associated with prominent periportal, portacaval, and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy. Subsequent endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) characterizes the pancreatic neck lesion as a mixed solid and cystic mass associated with a fistulous tract draining purulent exudate directly into the first portion of the duodenum.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma with Duodenal Invasion
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: An ill-defined mass in the pancreatic neck invading the adjacent duodenum associated with retroperitoneal adenopathy and severe constitutional wasting in an elderly patient was highly suspicious for advanced pancreatic malignancy; however, EUS-guided core biopsy showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with no malignant cells.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Biopsy of the pancreatic mass yielded necrotic inflammatory debris with small cellular foci and granulomas but no malignant cells.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Cystic Pancreatic Neoplasm / Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: A mixed solid and cystic pancreatic mass with regional adenopathy can represent a mucinous cystadenoma or cystic neuroendocrine neoplasm, but spontaneous duodenal fistulization with purulent drainage and caseous granulomas excluded a primary cystic neoplasm.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) characterized the pancreatic mass as mixed solid/cystic with a fistula draining purulent material into the first part of the duodenum.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: EUS-guided biopsy of the pancreatic lesion demonstrated positive acid-fast bacilli on histological staining, and tissue culture definitively grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex susceptible to first-line agents, confirming pancreatic tuberculous pseudotumor.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Acid-fast bacilli (AFB) stain was positive (Figure 1), and culture grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) complex, susceptible to rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol.

editor_comments: Admission clinical narrative stops after EUS visualization of the pancreatic mass and duodenal fistula, prior to biopsy, microbiological staining, HIV screening, and treatment. Direct verbatim quotes validated against case text.
